findings.statement: Bounded replay run:72cf0e4b91a3 (3 of 3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled; fan-in threshold 5 distinct senders per 1-hour event-time window; onward max gap 30 min) holds 55 transfers, 48 accounts, 35 devices, 14 onward links and 2 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset.

Alert fan_in:A-9278:1794301200000: account A-9278 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders between 1794301200000 and 1794304800000, 357000 minor units in total (T0002, T0003, T0006, T0010, T0011, T0012).
Alert fan_in:A-9895:1794319200000: account A-9895 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders between 1794319200000 and 1794322800000, 15000 minor units in total (T0035 to T0040, each 2500).

All six contributions to A-9278 are passed on. T0002, T0003 and T0006 link to T0007 (A-9278 to A-5092), then T0008 (A-5092 to A-2897), then T0009 (A-2897 to A-4989). T0010, T0011 and T0012 link to T0014, then T0015, then T0016 along the same accounts. Chains reach 3 onward links at most. The route is A-9278, A-5092, A-2897, A-4989, and the money comes to rest only at A-4989 (T0009 and T0016 are not passed on). Each hop is a little smaller than the one before: 138000, 135000, 132000 and 210000, 206000, 202000.

Only three of the six contributions to A-9895 are passed on. T0038, T0039 and T0040 link to T0041 (A-9895 to A-1415, 14000), which has no onward link. T0035, T0036 and T0037 have no onward link. Chains reach 1 onward link at most, the route accounts are A-9895 and A-1415, and the money comes to rest at A-1415. A-1415's later transfer T0055 (90000 to A-9514) is not recorded as an onward link, and T0055 itself is not passed on.

Shared devices on routes: for the A-9278 alert, device D-568 sent every recorded transfer from route accounts A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 (T0007, T0008, T0009, T0014, T0015, T0016). The resting account A-4989 sent nothing. For the A-9895 alert, no device was used by two or more route accounts: A-9895 sent from D-699 and A-1415 from D-785.

Both indicators have the same shape: 6 senders and 6 transfers in one hour. What sets them apart is the recorded relationships. A-9278 passes on every contribution through a 3-hop chain that ends at one account, and all three sending accounts on that route used one device (D-568). A-9895 passes on half its contributions in a single hop, no device is shared on its route, and its 6 contributions are small and identical (2500 each, 15000 in total, compared with 357000). So the A-9278 alert comes with corroborating relationships that go beyond the fan-in. The A-9895 alert rests mostly on the fan-in count alone.

hypotheses.statement: A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 might be run by one party or through one device, which would make the chain to A-4989 look like layering (pass-through accounts) of collected funds. Sharing a device does not prove ownership or identity, and the onward links are based on timing, not proof that the same money moved.

The A-9895 fan-in (six identical 2500 payments) could be ordinary collection activity, such as a shared bill or a pool, rather than mule activity. Its one-hop forwarding to A-1415 is weaker evidence than the A-9278 pattern.

A-1415's 90000 payment to A-9514 (T0055) is larger than anything A-1415 received in this dataset. That could point to funds from outside the dataset, or to a later stage of movement the 30-minute onward rule does not capture.

unresolved.question: Who controls A-4989, and what happened to the funds after they arrived there? The dataset records no outgoing transfer from A-4989.
Do D-568 sessions belong to one person or to a shared or aggregator device? The data records only device ids.
Where did the money A-1415 sent in T0055 come from, and was it connected to the A-9895 funds at all? It falls outside the onward gap, and its amount is more than A-1415 is recorded as receiving.

What happened to the A-9895 contributions that were not passed on (T0035, T0036, T0037)? The data cannot say whether they stayed in the account or left later through a payment the 30-minute onward rule does not link.
